topics.title: Solid shapes in monuments and models

learn.hook: India Gate, Qutub Minar and even your school building are made of solid shapes hiding in plain sight!
points: Big buildings are made of solid shapes: cuboids, cubes, cylinders, cones, spheres, prisms and pyramids.
Qutub Minar looks like tall cylinders stacked one on another, getting thinner at the top.
To build a model, pick the block whose shape matches each part: a cuboid for a wall, a cylinder for a pillar, a cone or pyramid for a pointed top.
A model looks like the real thing in shape, but it is much smaller and made of different material.
You can make a street model from waste: boxes for houses, bottles and tubes for towers, bottle caps for wheels.

example.q: Neha builds a model gate with blocks. She needs 2 tall pillars and a flat top piece across them. Which blocks should she choose?
steps: Pillars are tall and round or tall and straight: cylinders or long cuboids work.
The top piece is a long flat block lying across: a cuboid.
So 2 cylinders (or tall cuboids) and 1 long cuboid.
example.answer: 2 cylinders for the pillars and 1 long cuboid on top

learn.reallife: Next time you pass a temple, a water tank or a bus stop, name the solid shapes in it: the dome, the tank, the pillars and the roof.

games.title: Model or real?
items: A model of India Gate is smaller than the real India Gate.
Models are built small so they fit on a table.
A model must be made of the same stone as the real monument.
Models use blocks, clay, card or waste material.
A model and the real building can have the same shape.
The shape is copied; the size and material change.
An empty toothpaste box can be a house in a street model.
A box is a cuboid, just like many houses.
A plastic bottle can stand for a tall round tower in a model.
A bottle is roughly a cylinder.
Bottle caps are a good choice for the roof of a house.
Bottle caps are small round discs; they suit wheels better than roofs.

quiz.q: Qutub Minar is a tall tower that gets thinner as it goes up. Which solid shape do its round sections look like?
quiz.explain: Each round section of the tower is like a cylinder, and they are stacked one on another.
quiz.mistake: Thinks every tall building is a pyramid

quiz.q: Aman wants a pointed top for his model temple, with a square base. Which block should he use?
quiz.explain: A square pyramid has a square base and sides that meet at one point, just like a pointed temple top.
quiz.mistake: Does not match the shape of the part to the block

quiz.q: Which part of a street model could you make with an empty matchbox?
quiz.explain: A matchbox is a cuboid, like a small shop building.
quiz.mistake: Does not see that a matchbox is a cuboid

quiz.q: How is a clay model of India Gate DIFFERENT from the real India Gate?
quiz.explain: A good model copies the shape, but it is much smaller and made of different material.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a model changes the shape of the building

quiz.q: Riya builds a model tower with 3 cylinder blocks stacked on top of each other and 1 cone on the very top. How many blocks does she use?
quiz.explain: 3 cylinders and 1 cone make 4 blocks.
quiz.mistake: Forgets to count the cone on top

quiz.q: A round dome sits on top of a building. Which solid shape is a dome most like?
quiz.explain: A dome is round and curved all over, like half a ball (half a sphere).
quiz.mistake: Mixes up a dome with a cone

quiz.q: Kabir makes a street model from waste. Which waste item is best for the wheels of a toy bus?
quiz.explain: Bottle caps are round and flat, just like wheels.
quiz.mistake: Picks an item without thinking about its shape

quiz.q: For a model gate, Meena uses 2 pillars and 1 cuboid across the top. She makes 3 such gates. How many blocks does she need?
quiz.explain: Each gate needs 2 + 1 = 3 blocks. 3 gates need 3 × 3 = 9 blocks.
quiz.mistake: Counts only the pillars

teach.ask: Gappu wants to build a tiny India Gate with blocks. How should Gappu choose the blocks?
teach.praise: Wow, now my model looks just like the real gate, only tiny!
teach.nudge: But which block shape fits each part, and how is my model different in size?

learn.hook: Open up a sweet box and lay it flat. What shape do you get? That flat shape is called a net!
points: A net is a flat shape that can be folded to make a 3D shape.
The net of a cube has 6 squares. The net of a cuboid has 6 rectangles.
The net of a cylinder has 2 circles and 1 rectangle.
The net of a square pyramid has 1 square and 4 triangles.
The top view is what you see from straight above. The front view is what you see from the front.

example.q: A glass shaped like a cylinder stands on a table. What do you see from the top and from the front?
steps: From straight above, you see the round rim: a circle.
From the front, you see a straight side, top and bottom: a rectangle.
example.answer: Top view: circle. Front view: rectangle.

learn.reallife: Sweet boxes, gift boxes and toothpaste boxes are made by folding flat cardboard nets.

games.title: Match the net to its shape

items.text: The top view of a glass standing on a table is a ___.
The front view of a party cap standing on a table is a ___.
The top view of a dice on a table is a ___.
The front view of a glass standing on a table is a ___.

quiz.q: How many squares are there in the net of a cube?
quiz.explain: A cube has 6 square faces, so its net has 6 squares.
quiz.mistake: Forgets the top or bottom face

quiz.q: A net has 2 circles and 1 rectangle. What does it fold into?
quiz.explain: The rectangle rolls into the curved side and the 2 circles close the top and bottom. That is a cylinder.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any net with circles makes a cone

quiz.q: Aisha looks at a glass standing upright from straight above. What shape does she see?
quiz.explain: From the top she sees the round rim of the glass, which is a circle.
quiz.mistake: Gives the front view instead of the top view

quiz.q: A party cap shaped like a cone stands on its base. What is its front view?
quiz.explain: From the front, the cap goes from a wide bottom to a point at the top. It looks like a triangle.
quiz.mistake: Gives the top view (circle) instead of the front view

quiz.q: Kabir looks at a laddoo from the top, the front and the side. What shape does he see every time?
quiz.explain: A laddoo is a sphere. A sphere looks like a circle from every direction.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the view changes for a round ball

quiz.q: A net has 1 square and 4 triangles. What does it fold into?
quiz.explain: The square is the base and the 4 triangles fold up to meet at a point. That is a square pyramid.
quiz.mistake: Sees the square and thinks of a cube

quiz.q: Meena cuts open a cereal box shaped like a cuboid and lays it flat. How many rectangles are in the net?
quiz.explain: A cuboid has 6 faces: top, bottom, front, back and 2 sides. So the net has 6 rectangles.
quiz.mistake: Forgets the top and bottom faces

quiz.q: Harpreet looks at a dice lying on a table from straight above. What shape does she see?
quiz.explain: The top face of a dice is a square, so the top view is a square.
quiz.mistake: Guesses without picturing the top face

teach.ask: Gappu has a flat piece of card with squares on it. How can it become a box? And what is a top view?
teach.praise: Yes! A net folds up into a solid shape, and a view is what you see from one side. Gappu will make a box now!
teach.nudge: What do we do to a flat net to make it a 3D shape?

learn.hook: A camping tent and a tent-shaped chocolate bar are both prisms. The great tombs of Egypt are pyramids. What makes them different?
points: A prism has two matching end faces (bases) joined by rectangle side faces.
A pyramid has one base. Its side faces are triangles that meet at one point called the apex.
We name them by the shape of the base: triangular prism, square pyramid, pentagonal prism and so on.
A cube is a special prism: all 6 of its faces are equal squares.
You can make prisms and pyramids by folding their nets and sticking the edges.

example.q: A solid has 2 pentagon faces and 5 rectangle faces. What is it called?
steps: Two matching end faces joined by rectangles means it is a prism.
So it is a pentagonal prism.

learn.reallife: A camping tent is a triangular prism. A pencil box is a rectangular prism (cuboid). The roof of some temples is a pyramid.

games.title: Prism or pyramid?
items: Side faces are triangles meeting at a point

quiz.q: How many triangle side faces does a square pyramid have?
quiz.explain: A square base has 4 sides. Each side has one triangle on it, so there are 4 triangles.
quiz.mistake: Counts the base as a triangle too

quiz.q: What shape are the side faces of a prism?
quiz.explain: In a prism, the two bases are joined by rectangle side faces.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up prisms with pyramids, whose side faces are triangles

quiz.q: Which solid has all its faces as equal squares?
quiz.explain: A cube is a special prism with 6 equal square faces.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a cuboid always has square faces

quiz.q: A pyramid has a hexagon as its base. How many triangle faces does it have?
quiz.explain: A hexagon has 6 sides, so there are 6 triangles, one on each side.
quiz.mistake: Adds the base to the count of triangles

quiz.q: How many faces does a triangular prism have in all?
quiz.explain: It has 2 triangle bases and 3 rectangle sides: 2 + 3 = 5 faces.
quiz.mistake: Counts only the rectangles or only the bases

quiz.q: Ravi folds a net made of 1 triangle in the middle and 3 triangles around it. What does he make?
quiz.explain: A triangle base with 3 triangles that meet at the top makes a triangular pyramid.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any net with triangles makes a prism

quiz.q: The point where all the triangle faces of a pyramid meet is called the...
quiz.explain: The top point of a pyramid where the triangles meet is the apex.
quiz.mistake: Confuses the apex with the base

quiz.q: A prism has two pentagon bases. How many rectangle faces join them?
quiz.explain: Each side of the pentagon is joined by one rectangle, so there are 5 rectangles.
quiz.mistake: Counts all faces instead of only the rectangles

teach.ask: Gappu thinks a prism and a pyramid are the same thing. Can you explain the difference?
teach.praise: Two bases and rectangles for a prism, one base and triangles for a pyramid. Got it!
teach.nudge: What shape are the side faces of each, and how many bases do they have?

topics.title: Solid 3D shapes: faces, edges and corners

learn.hook: A laddoo rolls, but a dice does not. Why? Let us find out!
points: A 3D shape is solid. It has length, width and height. You can hold it.
A face is a flat surface. An edge is where two faces meet. A corner is where edges meet.
A cube (like a dice) has 6 square faces, 12 edges and 8 corners.
A cuboid (like a brick) also has 6 faces, 12 edges and 8 corners.
A sphere (like a laddoo) is round all over. A cylinder (like a tin) has 2 flat faces and a curved surface. A cone (like a party cap) has 1 flat face and a pointed tip.

example.q: A matchbox is a cuboid. How many faces, edges and corners does it have?
steps: Count the flat faces: top, bottom, front, back, left, right = 6
Count the edges: 4 on top, 4 on the bottom, 4 standing = 12
Count the corners: 4 on top and 4 on the bottom = 8

learn.reallife: Your geometry box is a cuboid, a ball is a sphere, a pipe is a cylinder and an ice-cream cone is a cone.

games.title: Match the object to its 3D shape
True or false?
items: A cube has 6 square faces: top, bottom and 4 around.
A sphere is round all over, so it has no corners.
Its curved surface lets it roll when it lies on its side.
A cone has only 1 flat face, the circle at its bottom.
Every face of a cube is a square.
All 6 faces of a cube are equal squares.
4 edges on top, 4 on the bottom and 4 standing up make 12.

quiz.q: How many faces does a dice shaped like a cube have?
quiz.explain: A cube has 6 faces. That is why a dice has the numbers 1 to 6.
quiz.mistake: Counts only the faces that can be seen at one time

quiz.q: How many edges does a cube have?
quiz.explain: A cube has 4 edges on top, 4 on the bottom and 4 standing up. 4 + 4 + 4 = 12.
quiz.mistake: Counts corners (8) instead of edges

quiz.q: How many corners does a matchbox shaped like a cuboid have?
quiz.explain: A cuboid has 4 corners on top and 4 on the bottom. 4 + 4 = 8.
quiz.mistake: Counts faces (6) or edges (12) instead of corners

quiz.q: Which shape can roll in every direction and has no flat face?
quiz.explain: A sphere is curved all over. It has no flat face, so it rolls any way.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a cylinder has no flat faces because it can roll

quiz.q: A tin of oil is shaped like which 3D shape?
quiz.explain: A tin has a circle at the top, a circle at the bottom and a curved side. That is a cylinder.
quiz.mistake: Names the 2D circle face instead of the 3D shape

quiz.q: How many flat faces does a cylinder have?
quiz.explain: A cylinder has 2 flat circle faces, one at the top and one at the bottom. Its side is curved, not flat.
quiz.mistake: Counts the curved side as a flat face

quiz.q: Which 3D shape has one flat circle face and one pointed tip?
quiz.explain: A cone, like a party cap, has a circle at the bottom and a pointed tip at the top.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the cone and the cylinder

quiz.q: Joseph has 2 dice. How many faces do the 2 dice have altogether?
quiz.explain: Each dice has 6 faces. 6 + 6 = 12.
quiz.mistake: Counts the faces of only one dice

teach.ask: Gappu found a dice and a laddoo. How are these solid shapes different? Please explain!
teach.praise: Super! Faces, edges and corners help me tell solid shapes apart. Gappu is a shape expert now!
teach.nudge: What can Gappu count on a dice? Think about faces, edges or corners.

topics.title: Building solids with straws and clay

learn.hook: With straws and small clay balls you can build the skeleton of a cube, and discover a secret number pattern!
points: In a straw model, each straw is an edge and each clay ball is a corner.
A cube skeleton needs 12 straws and 8 clay balls. A square pyramid needs 8 straws and 5 balls.
For solids with only flat faces: faces + corners − edges = 2. For a cube: 6 + 8 − 12 = 2.
A solid with only flat faces needs at least 4 faces. So no such solid has exactly 3 flat faces.
Paper strips joined crossing at the top and bottom, then spread out, make a ball-like sphere.

example.q: Sana has 6 straws and 4 clay balls. Which solid skeleton can she make using all of them?
steps: A triangular pyramid has 6 edges and 4 corners.
So she can make a triangular pyramid.

learn.reallife: Builders first make a frame of iron rods and joints, just like a straw skeleton, before adding walls.

quiz.q: In a straw-and-clay model, what does each straw stand for?
quiz.explain: The straws make the lines of the skeleton, which are the edges.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up edges with corners

quiz.q: How many clay balls are needed to make the skeleton of a cube?
quiz.explain: A cube has 8 corners, so it needs 8 clay balls.
quiz.mistake: Uses the number of faces or edges instead of corners

quiz.q: How many straws are needed for the skeleton of a square pyramid?
quiz.explain: 4 straws make the square base and 4 more go up to the apex: 4 + 4 = 8.
quiz.mistake: Forgets the straws that go up to the apex

quiz.q: A triangular prism has 5 faces and 6 corners. Use faces + corners − edges = 2 to find its number of edges.
quiz.explain: 5 + 6 = 11, and 11 − edges = 2, so edges = 9.
quiz.mistake: Adds 2 instead of taking it away

quiz.q: A solid has 6 faces and 12 edges. How many corners does it have?
quiz.explain: faces + corners − edges = 2, so 6 + corners − 12 = 2. Corners = 8.
quiz.mistake: Forgets to use the pattern

quiz.q: Can a solid with only flat faces have exactly 3 faces?
options: No, it needs at least 4 faces
quiz.explain: Three flat faces cannot close up a solid. The smallest such solid, a triangular pyramid, has 4 faces.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any number of faces can close a solid

quiz.q: Dev has 12 straws and 8 clay balls. He uses all of them. Which skeleton does he make?
quiz.explain: A cube has 12 edges and 8 corners, matching 12 straws and 8 balls.
quiz.mistake: Matches only one of the two numbers

quiz.q: Pooja joins 4 long paper strips so they cross at the top and bottom, then spreads them out. What shape does she get?
quiz.explain: Strips crossing at top and bottom and bending outwards look like a ball, a sphere.
quiz.mistake: Thinks flat strips can only make flat shapes

teach.ask: Gappu has a bag of straws and clay balls. Explain how to build a cube and what the secret pattern is.
teach.praise: Faces plus corners minus edges is 2! My cube really follows the pattern!
teach.nudge: Which part is the edge, which is the corner, and what number does the pattern give?

learn.hook: Next time you play Ludo, look closely at the dice. Its numbers hide a magic total!
points: On a standard dice, the numbers on opposite faces always add up to 7.
So 1 is opposite 6, 2 is opposite 5, and 3 is opposite 4.
Each face touches 4 other faces along its edges. These are its neighbours (adjacent faces).
Only the opposite face does not share an edge with a face.
Faces you see together in one view are neighbours, so they cannot be opposite each other.

example.q: A dice shows 2 on top. What number is at the bottom?
steps: Top and bottom are opposite faces.

learn.reallife: In board games like Ludo and Snakes and Ladders, the dice is made fair by putting each number opposite its partner that makes 7.

games.title: Dice facts
items: On a dice, 3 and 4 are on opposite faces.
On a dice, 1 and 2 are on opposite faces.
The face with 5 touches the face with 1 along an edge.
5 is opposite 2, so it is a neighbour of 1.
Every face of a dice has 4 neighbours.
Of the 5 other faces, all except the opposite one share an edge.
You can see 1 and 6 together in one view of a dice.
1 and 6 are opposite faces, so they are never seen together.

quiz.q: A dice shows 4 on top. What number is on the bottom face?
quiz.explain: Opposite faces add up to 7, and 7 − 4 = 3.
quiz.mistake: Forgets that opposite faces add to 7

quiz.q: Which number is opposite 1 on a dice?
quiz.explain: 1 + 6 = 7, so 6 is opposite 1.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the next number is opposite

quiz.q: Rohan sees 1, 2 and 3 together on one view of a dice. What is the total of the three faces he cannot see?
quiz.explain: The hidden faces are 6, 5 and 4 (opposites of 1, 2, 3). 6 + 5 + 4 = 15.
quiz.mistake: Adds the faces that can be seen

quiz.q: Which face of a dice does NOT share an edge with the face showing 3?
quiz.explain: Only the opposite face does not touch it. 3 + 4 = 7, so 4 is opposite 3.
quiz.mistake: Thinks all faces touch each other

quiz.q: Which of these is a neighbour (shares an edge) of the face with 6?
quiz.explain: 6 is opposite 1, so every other face, including 2, touches 6.
quiz.mistake: Picks the opposite face as a neighbour

quiz.q: The top and bottom faces of a dice together always make what total?
quiz.explain: Top and bottom are opposite, and opposite faces always add to 7.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the total depends on how the dice lands

quiz.q: A cube has 6 colours. In 3 views, red is seen with blue, green, yellow and white. Which colour is opposite red if the 6th colour is black?
quiz.explain: Colours seen with red are its neighbours. The only colour never seen with red is black, so black is opposite.
quiz.mistake: Thinks faces seen together can be opposite

quiz.q: Two dice lie on a table. What is the total of the two bottom faces if the top faces show 5 and 6?
quiz.explain: Bottom of 5 is 2, bottom of 6 is 1. 2 + 1 = 3.
quiz.mistake: Adds the top faces instead

teach.ask: Gappu found a dice and wants to know the number hiding at the bottom. How can Gappu find it without lifting the dice?
teach.praise: Seven minus the top number! Now I can see through dice!
teach.nudge: What do opposite faces always add up to?

learn.hook: A cube, a cone and a ball walk into a sorting game. Which group does each one join?
points: We can sort solids by their faces: only flat faces, only a curved surface, or both flat and curved.
Two overlapping circles (a Venn diagram) help sort by two rules at once, like 'has square faces' and 'has triangle faces'.
A shape that fits both rules goes in the overlap in the middle. A shape that fits neither goes outside both circles.
The shapes of the faces tell solids apart: a cube has only squares; a square pyramid has a square and triangles.
Clues about faces, edges and corners can name a solid: 5 faces, 8 edges, 5 corners is a square pyramid.

example.q: Where does a square pyramid go if one circle is 'has square faces' and the other is 'has triangle faces'?
steps: It has a square base, so it fits the first circle.
It has triangle sides, so it fits the second circle.
It fits both, so it goes in the overlap.

learn.reallife: Shopkeepers stack tins (cylinders) and boxes (cuboids) differently. Balls go in a basket because they roll!

games.title: Guess the solid from the clues
pairs: 2 flat circles and a curved surface

quiz.q: Which solid has only a curved surface and no flat face?
quiz.explain: A sphere is curved all over. Cylinders and cones also have flat faces.
quiz.mistake: Forgets that cylinders and cones have flat faces

quiz.q: Which solid has BOTH flat faces and a curved surface?
quiz.explain: A cylinder has 2 flat circle faces and 1 curved surface.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a cylinder is only curved

quiz.q: In a Venn diagram, one circle is 'has square faces' and the other is 'has triangle faces'. Where does a triangular pyramid go?
quiz.explain: All 4 faces of a triangular pyramid are triangles. It has no square face, so it goes only in 'has triangle faces'.
quiz.mistake: Puts a shape in the overlap without checking both rules

quiz.q: Same circles: 'has square faces' and 'has triangle faces'. Where does a cylinder go?
quiz.explain: A cylinder has circle faces and a curved surface, so it fits neither rule and goes outside both circles.
quiz.mistake: Thinks every shape must go inside a circle

quiz.q: Which shape goes in the overlap of 'has square faces' and 'has triangle faces'?
quiz.explain: A square pyramid has a square base and triangle sides, so it fits both circles.
quiz.mistake: Picks a shape that fits only one rule

quiz.q: I have 6 faces. All of them are rectangles, and they are not all squares. What am I?
quiz.explain: 6 rectangle faces that are not all squares make a cuboid, like a brick.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up cube and cuboid

quiz.q: A solid has 4 faces, all triangles. What is it?
quiz.explain: A triangular pyramid has a triangle base and 3 triangle sides: 4 triangles in all.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a triangular prism has only triangles

quiz.q: How many of these have only flat faces: cube, cone, cuboid, sphere, square pyramid?
quiz.explain: Cube, cuboid and square pyramid have only flat faces. That is 3.
steps: Flat only: cube, cuboid, square pyramid
quiz.mistake: Counts the cone as having only flat faces

teach.ask: Gappu has a pile of solids and two hoops on the floor. How should Gappu sort them?
teach.praise: Shapes that fit both rules sit in the middle! Sorting is fun!
teach.nudge: Where do shapes go if they fit both rules, or neither rule?

topics.title: Cube towers, dot paper and net puzzles

learn.hook: Some cubes in a tower are hiding! Can you count the ones you cannot see?
points: When cubes are stacked, some cubes are hidden behind or below others. Count layer by layer.
A block 2 cubes long, 2 wide and 2 high has 2 × 2 × 2 = 8 cubes, even though one is hidden from view.
On triangular (isometric) dot paper, a cube is drawn with 3 faces showing: the top and two sides.
A cube net must have exactly 6 squares. 6 squares in one straight line will NOT fold into a cube.
If a net has only 5 squares, one face is missing and the box stays open.

example.q: Arjun builds a 2 by 2 square layer of cubes and puts 1 cube on top in the middle of one corner. How many cubes in all?

learn.reallife: Gift boxes and sweet boxes come flat from the factory as nets. The shopkeeper folds them up when you buy sweets.

games.title: Will it fold into a cube?
items: Folding a straight strip makes the ends overlap; it cannot close.
A cross shape: 4 squares in a column with one square on each side of the second square
This is a well-known cube net.
A cube needs 6 faces, so one face is missing.
A cube has exactly 6 faces; one square would be extra.
A T shape: 3 squares in a row on top, with 3 more squares going down from the middle one
The column of 4 wraps around and the two side squares close the ends.

quiz.q: A block is 2 cubes long, 2 cubes wide and 2 cubes high. How many cubes are in it?
quiz.explain: Each layer has 2 × 2 = 4 cubes. 2 layers make 8 cubes. One is hidden at the back.
quiz.mistake: Counts only the cubes that can be seen

quiz.q: In that 2 × 2 × 2 block, you can see 7 cubes. How many cubes are hidden?
quiz.explain: 8 cubes in all, 7 can be seen, so 8 − 7 = 1 is hidden.
quiz.mistake: Thinks what you see is all there is

quiz.q: A staircase has 4 cubes at the bottom, 3 in the next row, 2 next and 1 on top, all in one line from the front. How many cubes?
quiz.mistake: Counts only one row

quiz.q: When one cube is drawn on triangular dot paper, how many of its faces show in the drawing?
quiz.explain: The drawing shows the top and two sides, so 3 faces.
quiz.mistake: Thinks all 6 faces can be drawn

quiz.q: Which of these flat shapes will NOT fold into a cube?
options: 3 squares in a row with 3 more going down from the middle one
4 squares in a row with one square above and one below
quiz.explain: A straight line of 6 squares overlaps itself when folded and cannot close.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any 6 squares make a cube

quiz.q: Priya's cube net has only 5 squares. What will happen when she folds it?
quiz.explain: A cube needs 6 faces. With 5 squares, one face is missing, like an open box.
quiz.mistake: Does not count the faces needed

quiz.q: A square pyramid net is missing one triangle. How many triangles does it have now?
quiz.explain: A square pyramid net has 1 square and 4 triangles. One missing leaves 4 − 1 = 3.
quiz.mistake: Forgets that a piece was cut off

quiz.q: A tower is 3 cubes high. Next to it is a tower 2 cubes high. Behind both, hidden, is a tower of 4 cubes. How many cubes altogether?
quiz.explain: 3 + 2 + 4 = 9, including the hidden tower.
quiz.mistake: Leaves out the hidden cubes

teach.ask: Gappu built a tower and says, 'I can see 7 cubes, so there are 7.' Help Gappu count properly.
teach.praise: Oh! Some cubes were hiding behind. Now I count layer by layer!
teach.nudge: Are there cubes you cannot see? How can you count them?

learn.hook: Open a book a little, then a lot. The opening between the covers is an angle!
points: An angle is made where two lines or edges meet at a point.
Angles are all around us: the corner of a book, the hands of a clock, an open door, scissors.
Fold a paper once, then fold it again so the folded edge lies on itself. The corner you get is a right angle checker.
A right angle is a square corner, like the corner of a book, a door or a table.
On a dot grid, two lines going straight across and straight up from the same dot make a right angle.

example.q: How many angles are there in a square drawn on a dot grid?
steps: At each corner two sides meet and make an angle.
So it has 4 angles, all right angles.

learn.reallife: Carpenters check that the corners of a door frame are right angles, or the door will not shut properly!

items.text: An angle is made where two lines ___.
A right angle looks like the corner of a ___.
To make a right angle checker, fold a paper ___ times.

quiz.q: What is made where two straight lines meet at a point?
quiz.explain: When two lines meet at a point they make an angle.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up angles with shapes

quiz.q: How many angles does a triangle have?
quiz.explain: A triangle has 3 corners, and each corner is an angle.
quiz.mistake: Counts sides and corners together

quiz.q: How do you make a right angle checker from a piece of paper?
options: Fold it twice, the second fold along the first folded edge
quiz.explain: Fold once to get a straight edge, then fold that edge onto itself. The corner is a right angle.
quiz.mistake: Thinks one fold is enough

quiz.q: Which of these makes a right angle?
quiz.explain: At 3:00 the hands make a square corner, a right angle.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a straight line is a right angle

quiz.q: Zoya puts her right angle checker on the corner of her school bag tag. It fits exactly. What does this tell her?
options: The corner is a right angle
The corner is bigger than a right angle
The corner is smaller than a right angle
quiz.explain: If the checker fits exactly, the corner is a right angle.
quiz.mistake: Does not know how to use the checker

quiz.q: A drawing shows 2 triangles and 1 square. How many angles are there in all?
quiz.explain: Each triangle has 3 angles and the square has 4. 3 + 3 + 4 = 10.
quiz.mistake: Counts only the shapes

quiz.q: On a dot grid, Rahul draws a line straight across and another straight up from the same dot. What angle does he make?
quiz.explain: Across and straight up make a square corner, a right angle.
quiz.mistake: Thinks lines on a grid cannot make an angle

quiz.q: How many right angles does a rectangle-shaped blackboard have?
quiz.explain: A rectangle has 4 corners, and all 4 are right angles.
quiz.mistake: Thinks only a square has right angles

teach.ask: Gappu wants to know if the corner of the window is a right angle. How can Gappu check with just a paper?
teach.praise: I folded my paper twice and checked the window. It fits, so it is a right angle!
teach.nudge: How many times do you fold the paper, and what do you do with the corner you make?

learn.hook: Is the tip of your pizza slice sharp or wide? Angles come in three sizes!
points: An acute angle is smaller than a right angle, like the tip of a pizza slice.
An obtuse angle is bigger than a right angle but less than a straight line, like a wide-open hand fan.
Use your right angle checker: if the angle fits inside it, it is acute; if the angle is wider, it is obtuse.
Capital letters have angles too. V and A have acute angles. L has a right angle.
Clues about angles can name a shape: 4 sides, all right angles, and equal sides means a square.

example.q: Clock hands at 2:00. Is the angle acute, right or obtuse?
steps: At 3:00 the hands make a right angle.
At 2:00 the hands are closer together.
So the angle is smaller than a right angle: acute.

learn.reallife: A slide in the park, the open lid of a laptop, and a ladder against a wall all make angles of different sizes.

games.title: Guess the shape from angle clues
pairs: 4 right angles, only opposite sides equal
4 equal sides, 2 acute and 2 obtuse angles

quiz.q: An angle is smaller than a right angle. What type of angle is it?
quiz.explain: Angles smaller than a right angle are acute.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the names acute and obtuse

quiz.q: An angle is bigger than a right angle but less than a straight line. What is it called?
quiz.explain: Bigger than a right angle means obtuse.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up acute and obtuse

quiz.q: What type of angle do the clock hands make at 4:00?
quiz.explain: At 3:00 it is a right angle. At 4:00 the hands are wider apart, so the angle is obtuse.
quiz.mistake: Thinks bigger numbers on the clock give smaller angles

quiz.q: The angle at the bottom tip of the letter V is...
quiz.explain: The two lines of V meet in a sharp point, smaller than a right angle.
quiz.mistake: Thinks every angle in a letter is a right angle

quiz.q: Which capital letter has a right angle?
quiz.explain: The two lines of L meet in a square corner.
quiz.mistake: Thinks V or A has a right angle

quiz.q: Rani draws a line. She wants to draw an obtuse angle from one end. How should the second line go?
options: Opening wide, more than a square corner
On top of the first line
Very close to the first line
Straight up, making a square corner
quiz.explain: An obtuse angle opens wider than a right angle.
quiz.mistake: Draws an acute angle instead

quiz.q: A shape has 3 angles. One is a right angle and the other two are acute. What shape is it?
quiz.explain: Any shape with 3 angles is a triangle. This one is a right triangle.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a right angle means a square

quiz.q: A shape has 4 equal sides. Two angles are acute and two are obtuse. Which shape is it?
quiz.explain: 4 equal sides like a square, but pushed so the angles are not right angles: a rhombus.
quiz.mistake: Thinks equal sides always mean a square

quiz.q: Meera colours acute angles red, right angles blue and obtuse angles green. Her rhombus has 2 acute and 2 obtuse angles. How many angles are green?
quiz.explain: Obtuse angles are coloured green. The rhombus has 2 obtuse angles, so 2 are green (and 2 are red).
quiz.mistake: Colours by the number of sides instead of the angle type

teach.ask: Gappu calls every angle a 'corner'. Teach Gappu the three kinds of angles.
teach.praise: Acute is small, right is a square corner, and obtuse is wide. Super!
teach.nudge: What do we call angles smaller than and bigger than a right angle?

learn.hook: A rangoli tile, a kite and a roti are all flat shapes. Can you count their sides and corners?
points: A 2D shape is flat. You can draw it on paper.
A side is a straight line on the edge of a shape. A corner is where two sides meet.
Triangle: 3 sides. Square and rectangle: 4 sides. Pentagon: 5 sides. Hexagon: 6 sides.
A circle has one curved edge and no corners.
In a closed shape made of straight sides, the number of sides and corners is the same.

example.q: Kabir draws a hexagon and a triangle. How many sides do they have altogether?

learn.reallife: Look at floor tiles, a carrom board, road signs and a kite. Each one is a flat shape you can name by counting its sides.

games.title: Match the shape to its sides

quiz.q: How many sides does a hexagon have?
quiz.explain: A hexagon has 6 straight sides and 6 corners.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the hexagon with the pentagon or octagon

quiz.q: A rangoli tile has 5 straight sides. What is the name of this shape?
quiz.explain: A flat shape with 5 straight sides is a pentagon.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the names pentagon and hexagon

quiz.q: How many corners does a circle have?
quiz.explain: A circle has one curved edge and no corners at all.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the start point of a drawn circle is a corner

quiz.q: Riya joins 3 straight sticks end to end to make a closed shape. Which shape does she get?
quiz.explain: 3 straight sides joined in a closed shape make a triangle.
quiz.mistake: Does not link the number of sides to the shape name

quiz.q: Arjun draws 2 triangles and 1 square. How many sides is that altogether?
quiz.explain: Each triangle has 3 sides and the square has 4. 3 + 3 + 4 = 10.
quiz.mistake: Counts only one triangle

quiz.q: Which of these is a flat 2D shape?
quiz.explain: A square drawn on paper is flat. A ball, a dice and a tin are solid 3D objects.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any object with a square face is a 2D shape

quiz.q: Kabir draws a square with each side 5 cm long. What is the total length of all its sides?
quiz.explain: A square has 4 equal sides. 5 + 5 + 5 + 5 = 20 cm.
steps: A square has 4 sides of 5 cm
quiz.mistake: Adds only two sides, or multiplies 5 by 5

quiz.q: Meena counts all the corners of one square and one triangle. How many corners does she count?
quiz.explain: A square has 4 corners and a triangle has 3 corners. 4 + 3 = 7.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a triangle has 4 corners

teach.ask: Gappu is puzzled! How do I know if a flat shape is a triangle, a square or a hexagon?
teach.praise: Wow! Count the sides and corners and the shape tells you its name. Gappu gets it now!
teach.nudge: What should Gappu count on the shape to find its name?

learn.hook: Push a straw square and it squashes. Push a straw triangle and it stays strong. Why?
points: A triangle made of straws keeps its shape when pushed. It is rigid (strong).
A square or rectangle of straws can be pushed out of shape. Its sides stay the same, but its angles change.
Rectangles and squares are 4-sided shapes with all four angles right angles.
A 5-sided straw shape (pentagon) also changes its angles when pushed.
We can group shapes by how many angles they have: fewer than 5 (triangles, 4-sided shapes) or more than 5 (hexagons, octagons).

example.q: Mohan pushes a straw square at one corner. What changes and what stays the same?
steps: The straws do not stretch, so the side lengths stay the same.
The corners lean over, so the angles change.
The square becomes a slanted shape with 2 acute and 2 obtuse angles.
example.answer: Sides stay the same, angles change

learn.reallife: Bridges, electric towers and bicycle frames use triangles because triangles do not bend out of shape.

games.title: Straw shape facts
items: A straw triangle keeps its shape when pushed.
Three fixed sides lock the triangle's angles.
A straw square keeps its right angles when pushed.
It leans over and its angles change.
Pushing a straw rectangle changes the lengths of its sides.
The straws stay the same length; only the angles change.
All four angles of a rectangle are right angles.
That is what makes it a rectangle.
A straw pentagon with equal sides can change its angles when pushed.
Like a square, it is not rigid.
A hexagon has fewer than 5 angles.

games.title: Fewer than 5 angles or more than 5?

quiz.q: Which straw shape stays firm and does not change shape when pushed?
quiz.explain: A triangle is rigid: its three sides lock its angles.
quiz.mistake: Thinks squares are the strongest shape

quiz.q: When a straw square is pushed at one corner, what changes?
quiz.explain: The straws stay the same length, but the angles change.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the sides stretch

quiz.q: What is true about all the angles of a rectangle?
options: Two are right and two are acute
quiz.explain: A rectangle has 4 right angles.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up a rectangle with a pushed shape

quiz.q: Why are electric towers built with many triangles?
options: Triangles keep their shape and make the tower strong
quiz.explain: Triangles are rigid, so the tower does not bend out of shape.
quiz.mistake: Does not link rigidity to strength

quiz.q: On a dot grid, Kavya draws a 4-sided shape with all right angles. Two sides are 3 dots apart and two are 5 dots apart. What is it?
quiz.explain: 4 right angles with opposite sides equal but not all sides equal: a rectangle.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any 4-sided shape with right angles is a square

quiz.q: How many angles does a 5-sided shape have?
quiz.explain: A shape has as many angles as sides, so 5 angles.
quiz.mistake: Doubles the number of sides

quiz.q: Which shape has MORE than 5 angles?
quiz.explain: A hexagon has 6 angles. The others have 3 or 4.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up hexagon and pentagon

quiz.q: Arun draws a triangle, a square and a hexagon. How many of them have fewer than 5 angles?
quiz.explain: The triangle (3) and the square (4) have fewer than 5 angles. The hexagon has 6.
quiz.mistake: Counts the hexagon too

quiz.q: Hari makes a pentagon with 5 equal straws and pushes one corner. What happens?
options: The angles change but the sides stay the same length
quiz.explain: Like a square, a straw pentagon is not rigid. The straws keep their length, but the angles change when it is pushed.
quiz.mistake: Thinks every straw shape is rigid like a triangle

teach.ask: Gappu made a house of straws but the square walls keep leaning. What should Gappu add and why?
teach.praise: I added a straw across to make triangles. My house stands firm now!
teach.nudge: Which shape keeps its shape, and what changes when a square is pushed?

topics.title: Amazing circles: centre, radius and diameter

learn.hook: Put many equal straws around one point and their ends trace a perfect circle. Magic? No, maths!
points: Every point on a circle is the same distance from its centre, the middle point.
You can draw a circle by marking many points at the same distance from a centre and joining them smoothly.
The radius is a line from the centre to the edge. The diameter is a line across the circle through the centre.
Fold a circle in half to find a diameter. All diameters meet at the centre and are equal.
Diameter = 2 × radius. Radius = half of the diameter.

example.q: A bicycle wheel has spokes 30 cm long from the centre to the rim. How wide is the wheel across the middle?
steps: A spoke from centre to rim is a radius: 30 cm.
Across the middle is the diameter.

learn.reallife: Bangles, wheels, rotis and round rangoli designs are all circles. A round carpet design has a centre with lines going out like radii.

games.title: Circle words
pairs: Edge to edge through the centre

quiz.q: A circle has a radius of 6 cm. What is its diameter?
quiz.explain: The diameter is twice the radius: 2 × 6 = 12 cm.
quiz.mistake: Halves the radius instead of doubling

quiz.q: A round roti is 20 cm across through the centre. What is its radius?
quiz.explain: 20 cm across is the diameter. Radius = 20 ÷ 2 = 10 cm.
quiz.mistake: Doubles the diameter instead of halving

quiz.q: Sunita folds a paper circle exactly in half. What does the fold line show?
quiz.explain: A fold that splits a circle into two equal halves passes through the centre. It is a diameter.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the fold is a radius

quiz.q: Two different diameters are drawn on one circle. Where do they cross?
quiz.explain: Every diameter passes through the centre, so all diameters meet there.
quiz.mistake: Does not know diameters pass through the centre

quiz.q: Kiran puts 8 straws, each 10 cm long, around a point like the spokes of a wheel. Their outer ends lie on a circle. Why?
options: Every end is the same distance, 10 cm, from the centre
quiz.explain: All points of a circle are the same distance from the centre. Equal straws put every end at 10 cm.
quiz.mistake: Does not see that equal distance makes a circle

quiz.q: Wheel A has a radius of 35 cm. Wheel B has a diameter of 60 cm. Which wheel is bigger?
quiz.explain: Wheel A's diameter is 2 × 35 = 70 cm, which is more than 60 cm. So A is bigger.
quiz.mistake: Compares a radius with a diameter directly

quiz.q: A round carpet has a design line from its centre to its edge that is 75 cm long. What is the carpet's diameter?
quiz.explain: Centre to edge is the radius. Diameter = 2 × 75 = 150 cm.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the radius is the full width

quiz.q: How many diameters can be drawn in a circle?
quiz.explain: You can draw a diameter through the centre in any direction, so there are very many, all equal.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a circle has only one diameter

quiz.q: Asha has no compass. She wants to draw a circle of radius 5 cm. She marks a centre dot. What should she do next?
options: Draw a square around the dot
Mark one point 5 cm away and stop
Mark many points 5 cm from the dot and join them smoothly
quiz.explain: Every point of a circle is the same distance from the centre. Many points 5 cm from the dot, joined smoothly, make the circle.
quiz.mistake: Does not see that all points of a circle are the same distance from the centre

teach.ask: Gappu found a round bangle and asks, 'What are radius and diameter?' Explain to Gappu.
teach.praise: Radius goes from the centre to the edge, and the diameter is twice as long. My bangle makes sense now!
teach.nudge: Where does the radius start, and how is the diameter related to it?

topics.title: Shape puzzles: hidden shapes, cuts and paths

learn.hook: A square with both its diagonals drawn hides 8 triangles. Can you find them all?
points: Big pictures hide smaller shapes. Look for shapes made of one piece, then of two or more pieces together.
One diagonal cuts a square into 2 triangles. Both diagonals cut it into 4 triangles.
A triangle can be cut on a dot grid into a square and smaller triangles.
To count all triangles, count small ones first, then the bigger ones made by joining pieces.
To trace a figure without lifting your pencil or repeating a line, start at a point where an odd number of lines meet.

example.q: A triangle has one line drawn from its top corner down to its base. How many triangles are there in all?
steps: The whole big triangle is also a triangle.

learn.reallife: Matchstick puzzles, tangram sets and kolam patterns are all fun shape puzzles. Kolam artists draw some patterns in one go without lifting their hand!

items.q: Square with both diagonals: small ones
Triangle with 1 line from the top

games.title: Puzzle facts
items: One diagonal cuts a square into 2 triangles.
The diagonal joins opposite corners and makes 2 triangles.
A square with both diagonals has only 4 triangles.
4 small ones plus 4 bigger ones made of two small ones: 8.
To make 2 triangles side by side you need 6 matchsticks.
They share one stick, so 5 are enough.
A rectangle can be cut into 2 smaller rectangles with one straight cut.
Cut straight across, parallel to a side.

quiz.q: A square has one diagonal drawn. How many triangles do you see?
quiz.explain: The diagonal joins opposite corners and cuts the square into 2 triangles.
quiz.mistake: Counts the square as a triangle

quiz.q: A square has BOTH diagonals drawn. How many triangles are there in all?
quiz.explain: 4 small triangles, plus 4 bigger triangles each made of 2 small ones: 4 + 4 = 8.
quiz.mistake: Counts only the small triangles

quiz.q: A triangle has 2 lines drawn from its top corner to its base. How many triangles are there in all?
quiz.explain: 3 small triangles, 2 made of 2 small ones next to each other, and 1 big one: 3 + 2 + 1 = 6.
quiz.mistake: Counts only the small triangles

quiz.q: Leela has 5 matchsticks. How many triangles can she make side by side, sharing sticks?
quiz.explain: The first triangle needs 3 sticks. The second shares a side and needs only 2 more: 3 + 2 = 5.
quiz.mistake: Thinks each triangle needs 3 new sticks

quiz.q: A row of 3 triangles side by side is made with 7 matchsticks. If you remove one outer stick of the last triangle (a stick it does not share), how many triangles are left?
quiz.explain: Removing a side of the end triangle breaks it, leaving 2 triangles.
quiz.mistake: Thinks removing a stick removes all triangles

quiz.q: Ankit cuts a square on a dot grid along one diagonal. What two shapes does he get?
quiz.explain: A diagonal cut joins opposite corners and makes 2 triangles.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a diagonal cut makes rectangles

quiz.q: A big right-angled triangle has a square cut out at its right-angled corner. The far corner of the square just touches the slanting side. What shapes are left over?
quiz.explain: When a square is cut from the corner of a triangle, the leftover pieces are smaller triangles.
quiz.mistake: Does not see the pieces left over

quiz.q: Diya wants to trace a square with one diagonal without lifting her pencil or going over a line twice. Where should she start?
options: In the middle of a side
At a corner where 3 lines meet
At a corner where 2 lines meet
quiz.explain: The two ends of the diagonal have 3 lines each. Start at one of them and finish at the other.
quiz.mistake: Starts at a point with an even number of lines

quiz.q: A drawing of a house has a square wall, a triangle roof, a rectangle door and a round window. How many different kinds of shapes are hidden in it?
quiz.explain: Square, triangle, rectangle and circle: 4 different kinds of shapes.
quiz.mistake: Misses one of the shapes in the picture

teach.ask: Gappu says there are only 4 triangles in a square with both diagonals. How do you help Gappu count them all?
teach.praise: 4 small and 4 big ones, 8 triangles! I will never miss hidden shapes again.
teach.nudge: Did you count the bigger triangles made by joining small ones?
